Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

multibayes 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • pd.adjust() reports the threshold c* that pd must reach (attr(x, "threshold.adj")): a claim is made only if its posterior probability is at least c under every prior in a class that lowers the prior odds of either direction, which is equivalent to pd >= c*.
  • pd.adj has a new meaning: it is the posterior probability of the claimed direction under the prior in the class most skeptical of it, so that the other side has probability 1 - pd.adj under the same prior. It is no longer floored at 0.5, and pd.adj >= c is the same rule as pd >= c*.
  • joint() now returns objects of class joint_directional (default) or joint_interval (interval = TRUE). Both are still data frames.

Other changes

  • Directions are claimed when pd.adj >= c (equivalently pd >= c*), the analogue of p <= alpha; the printed rule and the documentation say so.
  • The simultaneous intervals of joint(interval = TRUE) are described by their joint posterior probability (prob), not as coverage.
  • pi0 is an upper bound, set by the researcher, on the prior probability of either sign of a parameter; p0 is the largest prior probability that no claim in the family is correct.
  • Values of pi0 below 0.5 (including those implied by p0) are set to 0.5, with a warning, so that no penalty is applied; pi0 = 0.5 is accepted without a warning.
  • Clearer printed output: the header of pd.adjust() shows only m, pi0, and the thresholds c and c*; null.value and direction, when they are the same for every test, are reported once in the header rather than as columns, so that tables fit on one line. joint() results print in the same way.
  • Clearer warning when direction is supplied together with pd.

multibayes 0.1.0
